newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar finishes quiet session little changed.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar finishes quiet session little changed.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar finished a quiet day's trading little changed on Monday with predictions it would trade gently lower in the near term.
One Wellington bank chief dealer said it had been unable to break above 70 U.S. cents since last Thursday's Reserve Bank easing statement.
"I think it will continue to test the bottom of the range," he said, adding that that could be US$0.6940-90 overnight.
It ended at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) at US$0.6975/82, much the same as its opening level and Friday's local close after trading a session range of 0.6967-00.
The Trade-Weighted Index ended one basis point higher at 68.42.

Stronger than expected retail sales data for January and robust housing inflation in the Real Estate Institute's latest figures was likely to see a tighter monetary policy mix than the Reserve Bank signalled it wanted on Thursday. Higher interest rates would underpin the currency, dealers said.
